newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iranian opposition in Iraq says attacked by gunmen.
newsitem.headline: Iranian opposition in Iraq says attacked by gunmen.

text.p: An Iranian exile group based in Iraq said on Wednesday Iranian "terrorists" attacked one of its vehicles north of Baghdad with anti-tank missiles and machineguns, wounding one of its members.
The group said the attack occurred on Tuesday evening when the car was travelling from Khalis 100 km (60 miles) from Baghdad to a nearby opposition Mujahideen Khalq military training camp.
The attackers fled in their car when the Mujahideen returned fire, leaving behind their weapons, the group said.

"At 6.30 pm on Tuesday terrorists sent by the mullahs' regime attacked a Mujahideen passenger car near Khalis with RPG- 7 anti-tank missiles, machine-guns and grenades. The Mujahideen in the car immdediately returned fire, forcing the assailants to escape," the organisation said in a statement handed to foreign reporters in Baghdad.
"The Mujahideen's car was damaged in the attack and one of the passengers suffered light injures," the exile group said.
The Mujahideen, which oppose the Tehran government, blamed what it called "the regime's intelligence ministry and terrorist diplomats" in the Iranian embassy in Iraq.
The statement quoted the group leader, Massoud Rajavi, as urging the Iraqi government to "prosecute, put on trial and punish the mullahs' terrorist diplomats and to shut down the embassy in Baghdad."
The group said this attack was the 42nd on the Mujahideen in Iraq.
The organisation uses Iraq as a springboard for attacks inside Iran and has several camps, equiped with heavy weapons, close to the borders with Iran.
Their bases have been the target of air and rocket attacks by Iran and their office in Baghdad, now ringed with a concrete wall, has weathered several mortar and bomb attacks.
